newsitem.title: USA: Clinton calls Netanyahu talk "frank, candid".
newsitem.headline: Clinton calls Netanyahu talk "frank, candid".

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Monday he and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had a "very specific, frank, candid and long talk" on the stalled Middle East peace prospects but he could say no more until he had spoken with the Palestinians.

"We had a very specific, frank candid and long talk. And now we're going to talk to the Palestinians and see whether there's something we can do to get this thing going again," Clinton told reporters after a meeting of about two hours with Netanyahu.

"The problem is, the more I comment the more I undermine chances of success," Clinton told reporters an another White House event that followed the Netanyahu meeting. "... I'm going to do my best to get it (the peace process) back on track."

The Netanyahu visit was arranged hastily in hopes reviving Israeli-Palestinian peace talks that have been disrupted by angry Arab reaction to Israel's decision to build new Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem, and by Israeli demands for a halt to Arab attacks on Israelis.

Netanyahu said before the meeting that Israel considered the housing construction a right that it had no intention of stopping. He declined to answer questions from White House reporters after his talk with Clinton.

"This was a profoundly serious meeting, profoundly serious enough that we're going to say very little about it," White House press secretary Mike McCurry said. He said Clinton expected to talk with a Palestinian delegation later this week, and added that he thought Clinton had given Netanyahu "some serious things to think about."
